preToolUse.description: Block shell commands that destroy history, bypass safety gates, overwrite live working-tree edits, discard stashed work, or stage by wildcard. Each entry carries a `concept` (the pattern family it is a fingerprint of), a `citation` (the doctrinal anchor), and a `reappraisal` (the positive direction the firing signals) so the deny message TEACHES: it names a concept to reappraise and steers the agent away from reaching for a sibling destructive command, rather than only refusing (PDR-044 §Innate immunity, as amended; the doctrine that an enforcement surface must carry the advisory-response content, not only a refusal). The five concepts: `history-destruction` (`git push --force` / `-f`, `git rebase -i`); `gate-bypass` (`git --no-verify`, `git --no-gpg-sign`); `worktree-destruction` (`git reset --hard`, `git clean -fd`, checkout/restore variants — these silently throw away in-flight edits, including peer-agent edits in parallel sessions, and `git fsck --lost-found` cannot recover them); `stash-discard` (`git stash drop` / `clear`); `wildcard-staging` (`git add -A` / `--all` / `.`, blocked under the explicit-pathspec discipline so a commit cannot accidentally bundle parallel-thread or unrelated work). We never use git to remove work; forward-going filesystem changes only. Entries may be bare strings (legacy) or objects; `concept` and `reappraisal` are optional at load time so a missing value never fails the guard closed (which would brick the worktree on a stale-dist/new-policy mismatch — a stale Bash guard blocks every command including the rebuild), and the `validate-policy-reappraisal` repo validator enforces their presence on object entries at commit-time. See `.agent/rules/never-use-git-to-remove-work.md`, `.agent/rules/no-verify-requires-fresh-authorisation.md`, and `.agent/rules/stage-by-explicit-pathspec.md`.

preToolUseContent.description: Block agents from writing into Edit/Write content. Two surfaces: (blocked_patterns) the owner-approval marker, path-agnostic, which only the project owner may author; (scoped_blocks) path-scoped doctrine block GROUPS per PDR-044 §Innate immunity. Each group gathers the surface patterns for one concept and carries the doctrinal `citation` PLUS a `reappraisal` — the positive direction the firing signals — so a block teaches the agent to step back and re-assess the concept rather than to reword around the wall (PDR-044 §Innate immunity, as amended; the doctrine that an enforcement surface must carry the advisory-response content, not only a refusal). `kind` and the `excludes_*` options are group-level: every pattern in a group shares them. The three concepts: (literal) `expediency-hedging` — language that means 'I know the rule applies, but this situation is special' rejected on doctrine surfaces (PDRs, plans, ADRs, governance), with doctrine-defining surfaces excluded so principles.md, distilled.md, PDR-043/044/047 may catalogue the words they forbid; (regex) `sha-in-permanent-doc` — 7- to 40-character hex tokens with at least one a-f character on portable-permanent-doc paths (practice-core, rules, memory/active/patterns, principles.md, testing-strategy.md; ADRs are repo-bound and out of scope per PDR-079), with fenced code blocks, inline-code spans, and `(historical reference)` marker lines excluded; (literal) `menu-framing` — owner-decision phrasings rejected on architectural surfaces so menu-shaped option-sets do not slip past the re-apply-first-question-at-elaboration-boundaries discipline (the rule file itself is excluded so it may catalogue the phrases it forbids). `reappraisal` is enforced present at commit-time by the `validate-policy-reappraisal` repo validator; it is optional at load time so a missing value never fails the guard closed. PDR-044 names false positives as a design property of the innate layer.
